articles.title: Dallas Cowboys All-Pro LG Tyler Smith To Miss 4-6 Weeks Due To Thumb Surgery
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith will undergo thumb surgery and is expected to be placed on injured reserve, likely missing the first 4-6 weeks of the season.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys' high-powered offense took a bit of a blow less than a week before their season-opening matchup against the New York Giants. All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith will undergo thumb surgery and is expected to be placed on injured reserve, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday. The surgery will force Smith to miss at least the first four games of the regular season while opening up a spot on the 53-man active roster. "Tyler Smith is going to have surgery on his thumb tomorrow morning," Schottenheimer said during his press conference. "It's something that he's just been dealing with." With Smith sidelined, offensive lineman T.J. Bass is slated to take over as the starting left guard. Bass joined the organization as an undrafted free agent and has made 10 career starts for Dallas, including five last year. The Cowboys retained Bass this offseason after placing a second-round restricted free agent tender on him. Smith's absence leaves a noticeable void in Dallas' offensive line. According to Pro Football Focus, Smith allowed just three sacks and 26 pressures last season. Since being selected in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft, the three-time Pro Bowler has allowed only 12 sacks across four seasons and 63 career starts, per PFF. Dallas opens the regular season on Sunday night against the Giants before rolling through an opening six-game stretch that includes matchups against the Washington Commanders, Baltimore Ravens, Houston Texans, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and Green Bay Packers.

articles.title: Panthers Optimistic Jonathon Brooks Plays Against Bears Despite Practice Absence
articles.summary: Carolina Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks missed his third straight practice with “general soreness," but coach Dave Canales remains hopeful he’ll be ready for Sunday’s season opener against the Chicago Bears
articles.body: Carolina's Jonathon Brooks missed his third straight practice with "general soreness," but Panthers coach Dave Canales remains hopeful the team's young running back will be ready for Sunday’s season opener against the Chicago Bears. Brooks spent time working on the side with trainers Monday while his teammates went through a short, non-padded practice. "We have to just keep taking it one day at a time," Canales said. "He ran out there today. We’ll see (where he is) and compare it to what he looked like before and we’ll go from there." Canales said last week he was "very optimistic" that Brooks would be able to play in Week 1. Brooks has missed 31 of 34 regular-season games since joining the Panthers, but the team remains high on his potential and believes he will be the perfect complement to starter Chuba Hubbard if he can stay healthy. The Panthers finished 19th in the league in rushing last season, averaging 116.3 points per game. They'll face a Bears defense that allowed 134.5 yards per game last season, which ranked 22nd in the league. "He's a guy who just makes plays in space down the field in the pass game, the screen game, and he has that the home run speed," Canales said. Canales said Brooks' speed can be deceiving. "Once he sets an angle, all of a sudden you see people start turning and realize he’s moving a lot faster than you think he is because he’s such a smooth, long strider," Canales said. "You don’t realize that. So, it’s a factor. It’s a pretty special dynamic in that regard." Brooks was not made available to reporters on Monday during the team's open locker room session. Panthers guard Damien Lewis said he likes Brooks' ability to hit the hole fast, saying he makes things easy on the team's offensive linemen since they don't have to hold their blocks as long. "He's really explosive," Lewis said. "When he gets that ball, he sees the space, he gone. So, you know, I call him one play action." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: How Much Is Florida State Coach Mike Norvell's Buyout? Contract Details In 2026
articles.summary: Florida State head coach Mike Norvell is on the hot seat early in the 2026 season following back-to-back losing years in Tallahassee.
articles.body: Florida State head coach Mike Norvell entered the 2026 college football season on the hot seat following back-to-back losing years in Tallahassee. After leading Florida State to a 13-0 regular season and an ACC championship in 2023, Florida State finished 2-10 in 2024 and 5-7 in 2025. Norvell holds an overall record of 38-34 at Florida State, including a 22-26 record in ACC play through six seasons. As FSU aims to meet fans and boosters' expectations, questions surrounding Norvell's contract and potential buyout details have emerged. What Is Mike Norvell's 2026 Salary? Norvell signed an eight-year contract extension prior to the 2024 season valued at more than $84 million through 2031, averaging roughly $10 million annually. Following the 2024 season, Norvell agreed to a restructured arrangement that directed $4.5 million toward institutional revenue-sharing initiatives. His contract includes a scheduled $150,000 salary increase each season. How Much Is Norvell's Buyout After This Season? If Florida State terminates Norvell without cause during or before the conclusion of the 2026 season, the university would owe him approximately $51 million, according to On3.com. If the decision occurs after the 2026 season, the buyout figure drops to roughly $45.6 million. According to On3.com, Norvell is owed 85% of his remaining salary and supplemental compensation. The buyout would reportedly be paid in monthly installments of approximately $800,000 through 2031 if fired after this season. What Is Florida State's Toughest Games And Remaining Schedule? Florida State opened the 2026 season with a home win over New Mexico State before taking on SMU. The remaining schedule includes a non-conference road contest at Alabama on Sept. 19 and the regular-season finale against rival Florida on Nov. 27 in Tallahassee. articles.title: 'Leon was apologising': How an illegal move cost Abhimanyu Mishra a sure-shot win in GCL
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: It was a dramatic start to Day 4 at the 2026 Global Chess League as the Ganges Grandmasters secured a 12-8 victory over the Alaskan Knights.
articles.body: BENGALURU: It was a dramatic start to Day 4 at the 2026 Global Chess League as the Ganges Grandmasters secured a 12-8 victory over the Alaskan Knights in a match defined by heartbreak, clock chaos, and a costly procedural blunder on the prodigy board.With the Alaskan Knights fighting for a match victory, prodigy Abhimanyu Mishra had successfully turned a drawn endgame against Leon Luke Mendonca into a winning attack.Down to mere seconds, Mishra executed a promotional sequence by capturing on f1 and promoting to a queen that immediately devolved into controversy.In his scramble to hit the clock, Mishra placed his new queen on the board while accidentally dropping the captured rook nearby, leaving both pieces cluttering the area.Arbiters deemed the move incomplete and illegal. Stripped of increment time, Mishra was forced to reset and retry the promotion with just one second remaining, causing him to flag instantly."I had two or three seconds after I played rook takes f1, g takes f1, promoting to a queen," Mishra told reporters post-game. "When I promoted, I took the queen and put the queen on the square, but somehow the rook was still in that area. The move wasn't entirely completed. I had to retry with one second left, and I flagged."The dramatic fault overturned what would have been a game-winning, and match-winning, triumph for his team."I saw the entire line... I won the queen," a gutted Mishra added. "If I won this game, we would've won the match as well. It was a very drawn position earlier, and I managed to start an attack. It really sucks. It hurts. What can I say?"Even Mendonca acknowledged the bitter nature of the point. "He (Leon) was apologising," Mishra said of his opponent. "This is not how anyone wants to win a game."Ganges' Levon Aronian weighed in on the chaotic sequence after the match, adding, "The confusion was that his opponent made an illegal move and pressed the clock... so they had to remove the two seconds from him. articles.title: Has Connor Bedard given the Chicago Blackhawks fresh hope with his return to the ice this NHL 2026-27 season
articles.summary: NHL News: Connor Bedard returns to the ice after shoulder surgery, raising hopes for the Chicago Blackhawks as they aim for NHL playoff contention this season.
articles.body: Connor Bedard was back on the ice for individual skating Monday, a good sign for the Chicago Blackhawks following his recovery from surgery on his left shoulder. The 20-year-old center skated on his own Monday at the Blackhawks Ice Center, another step in his rehabilitation.The development is especially notable because Chicago had earlier indicated Bedard would require about four months to recover from surgery. The injury occurred July 2 in an off-season workout in Vancouver, and the original timeline had him out until about November.Connor Bedard return lifts Blackhawks expectations The individual skating session should not be read as any indication that Bedard is ready to return to NHL game action. Rather, it’s a positive milestone on the road to rehabilitation for the Chicago Blackhawks, who are expected to take a measured approach with their franchise center.That he’s already able to skate, even if it’s relatively early in the recovery process, is nevertheless a positive sign for his progress. The Blackhawks still have to decide when he’s ready for contact, full practices and then competitive games.The timing also comes as Chicago prepares for a season of rising expectations. In each of his three NHL seasons, Bedard has been the Blackhawks’ top scorer, and in 2025-26 he had a career-high 75 points in 69 games.Connor Bedard remains central to Chicago’s NHL playoff hopesBedard’s health is particularly important to those ambitions, with the Blackhawks looking to take another step toward playoff contention heading into the offseason. The team has not made the Stanley Cup Playoffs in eight of the last nine seasons, including all three of Bedard’s first three NHL seasons.The Blackhawks have been preparing for his absence with players like Frank Nazar, Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi expected to step up with more offensive responsibilities early in the season. Bowen Byram is also expected to chip in some more offence from the blue line.With Bedard’s recent history, it’s a development to keep an eye on. He missed 12 games last season with a right shoulder injury and missed 14 games as a rookie after breaking his jaw. The left shoulder is the site of the injury this time.The immediate concern for the Blackhawks is still making sure Bedard gets himself back right, not rushing him back. His latest skating session is a welcome NHL injury update, but when he eventually gets back into game action will depend on how the shoulder responds through the next stages of rehab.Blackhawks’ Connor Bedard makes a return to the ice after left shoulder surgery, an encouraging update on his recovery. articles.title: Luis Díaz, nominado al Balón de Oro 2026: el colombiano compite por ser el mejor del mundo
articles.standfirst: Luis Díaz recibe su segunda nominación al Balón de Oro
articles.summary: Luis Díaz recibe su segunda nominación al Balón de Oro
articles.body: El nombre de Luis Díaz vuelve a escribirse con letras doradas en la historia del deporte colombiano y sudamericano. Este martes 8 de septiembre de 2026, la revista France Football reveló la lista oficial de los 30 futbolistas nominados al prestigioso Balón de Oro, galardón que distingue al mejor jugador del planeta en la temporada. Entre la selecta élite mundial reaparece el extremo guajiro, consolidando un presente excepcional que lo ratifica como una de las máximas figuras del balompié internacional. La inclusión de Díaz en el listado de candidatos no es producto del azar, sino el resultado lógico de una campaña sobresaliente (2025/2026) vistiendo los colores del Bayern Múnich. Tras su consolidación en la élite europea, el atacante colombiano dio un paso al frente en el gigante alemán, convirtiéndose en el motor ofensivo del equipo bávaro y en pieza fundamental para la consecución de los títulos de la Bundesliga, la Copa de Alemania y la Supercopa alemana. Los números respaldan con creces su candidatura. A lo largo del año competitivo, sumando compromisos con su club y la Selección Colombia, ‘Lucho’ disputó 60 partidos en los que firmó actuaciones memorables, aportando 28 goles y 21 asistencias. Su desborde vertiginoso, capacidad de asociación, sacrificio defensivo y peso en los momentos calientes de la temporada convencieron al panel de expertos de France Football para situarlo nuevamente entre los trenta mejores del mundo. El 2026 ha sido un año particularmente intenso y de consagración definitiva para el exjugador de Junior de Barranquilla y Porto. Además de dominar en el fútbol alemán, Luis Díaz asumió el liderazgo absoluto de la Selección Colombia, guiando al combinado nacional en la cita orbital del año y ratificando su jerarquía en los escenarios más exigentes del planeta. Su actuación en el torneo mundialista y en las fases definitivas con su club terminaron por pulir una candidatura que ya venía pronosticada por analistas internacionales desde finales de la temporada anterior. Esta se convierte en la segunda ocasión en que Luis Díaz aparece en la lucha por el Balón de Oro. La primera oportunidad data del año 2022, cuando su gran momento en el fútbol inglés le valió para entrar en la selecta lista y ocupar un meritorio puesto 17 a nivel mundial. Cuatro años después, el extremo da un salto cualitativo en su madurez futbolística, instalándose con argumentos sólidos en la pelea directa junto a los dominadores de la época. La ceremonia oficial en la que se conocerá al sucesor del trono y se entregarán los galardones definitivos está programada para el próximo lunes 26 de octubre de 2026. Mientras llega la fecha cumbre, Colombia celebra por doble partida, pues la presencia de Díaz en la categoría reina del Balón de Oro demuestra que el talento nacional sigue pisando fuerte en la cúspide del deporte rey, compitiendo de tú a tú contra las grandes chequeras y las máximas estrellas del firmamento futbolístico actual.

articles.title: How eye patches helped Mike Matthews catch two TD passes for Tennessee football
articles.summary: Tennessee assistant coach Kelsey Pope had a vision of how to make his wide receivers even better by covering one of their eyes.
articles.body:
Tennessee wide receivers coach Kelsey Pope was already returning one of the SEC's best units, but he had a vision of how to make them even better.

Specifically, that vision meant blinding one eye of each of his wide receivers.

"I watched a podcast that was talking about triggering different segments of the brain by covering one eye," Pope said on Sept. 8. "We bought about 25 eye patches, covered one eye and caught 1,000 balls."

An eye patch is an unorthodox tool to train for the 2026 season. But Pope has already seen gains as No. 18 Tennessee (1-0) prepares to play Georgia Tech (0-1) on Sept. 12 (7 p.m. ET, ESPN) at Bobby Dodd Stadium in Atlanta.

Tennessee football vs Furman in Faizon Brandon's debut: See our best photos

How eye patches aided Mike Matthews' TD catches

During the offseason, wide receivers caught footballs while wearing eye patches. It helped them focus on passes under less-than-ideal circumstances.

Pope believes it helped Mike Matthews catch two touchdown passes against Furman in Week 1.

When quarterback Faizon Brandon 's play-action fake sucked a safety toward the line of scrimmage, Matthews broke wide open. But Brandon's pass was headed directly over the head of Matthews, so he adjusted his route and caught it at a sharp angle over his shoulder for a 55-yard TD.

Brandon tossed another deep pass to Matthews, who outjumped a Furman defender to snag a 57-yard TD. He had to keep his eye on the football while fighting off the coverage.

Both were examples of passes that Matthews may have dropped earlier in his career. Pope said Matthews' hard work made the difference, including reps with those eye patches.

"The touchdown catches are a testament to Mike and something we really focused on this summer, which was eliminating drops," Pope said. "It wasn't a hand-eye coordination issue. It was more of a focus issue. So we worked on a lot of things this summer and got creative (with eye patches).

"It's a testament to him that when he does the work, the easier things will be."

This wide receiver competition is still wide open

Tennessee receivers were pretty reliable in the 56-9 win over Furman. Matthews dropped a short pass on fourth-and-3. But he also had a career-high 132 yards receiving.

Brandon praised his supporting cast for helping him complete 13 of 17 passes for 226 yards and three TDs in his debut.

The next step for UT wide receivers involves trimming the rotation. Matthews and Braylon Staley are locked in as one of the SEC's best receiving duos returning this season.

Sophomore Radarious Jackson started against Furman. But he's competing with sophomore Travis Smith and five-star freshman TK Keys for the third wide receiver spot. Pope said that battle is ongoing.

"It's still No. 3 by committee right now, which is a luxury," Pope said. "We've got three guys right now that we feel good about playing in that (third starting) spot. Nobody has necessarily taken a jump. But they're really building on one another, which is what we want in that room."

Jackson had three catches for 38 yards, and Pope was pleased with his blocking on rushing plays. Smith had two catches for 22 yards. Keys had two receptions for 29 yards, catching a 22-yard TD from George MacIntyre .

articles.title: Jerry Jones hints Cowboys eyeing another major trade: 'We're in play'
articles.summary: The Cowboys may be looking to add more veteran help, with owner Jerry Jones calling some recent moves "pretty conspicuously obvious."
articles.body:
The Cowboys are five days away from kicking off their 2026 regular season schedule, but don't assume that the 53-man roster as it exists right now is the way it's going to stay. The front office likes to say that talent acquisition is a 365-day-a-year endeavor... and in that regard, the Tuesday before the season opener is no different from any other day of football business.

In fact, owner Jerry Jones is hinting that the Cowboys still could have a major trade- or two- up their sleeve, even as the season begins to unfold.

"What's top of mind for me right now," Jones told Shan and RJ of 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday , "is getting the best team we can put on this field."

And that could mean spending some next year's draft capital early. The Cowboys currently have five picks in 2027, but Jones says he wouldn't hesitate to trade some portion of that haul- even at the high end- for the right player right now.

"Not at all," he said plainly. "You want all the picks you can get, but this time of the year, what you're interested in is what you're doing with the picks that you used and what you might be able to do if you could add to bringing talent on the roster. We're still alive and well in that area."

Indeed, the team elected not to simply stand pat after culling the training camp roster down to 53. They did a late-August deal with Pittsburgh for former first-round lineman Broderick Jones, who is expected to compete for a starting role.

And then in the first few days of September, they restructured the contracts of DaRon Bland, Kenny Clark, and Jake Ferguson to create $30 million of cap space. Such financial maneuvering could certainly be an important step toward taking on a veteran player with a significant contract... maybe very soon.

"The timing is pretty conspicuously obvious," Jones acknowledged. "We could use it for this year's team. The cap is fungible, and it laps over into multi-years: at least two, conceivably three or four, on parts of any money that you make available. That's hard to put your finger on. But that does show that we have really viable, serious room financially to make a trade if we wanted to right now."

Jones has teased "substantive" talks with at least one other unnamed team since mid-summer. So is a deal for a blockbuster player imminent?

"The best way for me to answer that is not timing-wise, right on something this morning or this week," Jones said. "But if you look at it, generally speaking, we're in play. And that's the best way to describe it."

Jones explained that he is happy with the team's firepower on offense, pointing to strong and fairly deep groups at quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and tight end. And even with the late-breaking temporary loss of three-time Pro Bowler Tyler Smith, don't expect the Cowboys to make a panicked move to add any more beyond Jones at offensive line.

So that means he's looking at the other side of the ball.

"You could look for it to be defensively," Jones suggested. "Defense would be the place."

articles.title: Anne Hathaway, Paul Rudd, Glen Powell, Jon Hamm, Larry David highlight Hollywood stars in Peyton, Eli Manning's ManningCast: Heist
articles.summary: Anne Hathaway, Paul Rudd, Glen Powell, Jon Hamm and Larry David headline a massive group of Hollywood stars joining Peyton Manning and Eli Manning for their...
articles.body:
Anne Hathaway , Paul Rudd, Glen Powell , Jon Hamm and Larry David headline a massive group of Hollywood stars joining Peyton Manning and Eli Manning for their latest "ManningCast" schedule reveal.

Alex Weprin of The Hollywood Reporter reported Tuesday that the actors appear in "ManningCast: Heist," an "Ocean's Eleven"-style short film from Omaha Productions that reveals the schedule for the sixth season of the alternate "Monday Night Football" broadcast. The roughly 15-minute production features about 40 cameos spanning A-list actors, current and former NFL players and NFL commissioner Roger Goodell.

"The tone of the heist is sort of a larger metaphor for the show itself," Omaha Productions president Jamie Horowitz told The Hollywood Reporter. "The Manningcast is meant to be a safe space, a show where everybody can just come on and talk about a love of football."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

According to Weprin, Omaha began planning the schedule reveal in late 2024 before production started in early 2025 at the Pro Bowl, allowing the company to begin securing its lengthy list of cameos. Omaha head of production Therese Andrews credited writer and producer DJ Gallo with developing the heist concept.

Powell's involvement also continues his connection with the Mannings through "Chad Powers." Powell stars in the comedy series inspired by the Chad Powers character Eli created for an episode of ESPN's "Eli's Places," with Peyton and Eli among the executive producers through Omaha Productions.

ESPN's Kalan Hooks provided additional details Tuesday about the plot of "ManningCast: Heist" and spoke with Peyton and Eli about the production. The story begins when Peyton discovers that the ManningCast has a Week 6 game scheduled on the same night as his book club. Eli suggests asking Goodell to change the schedule, but Peyton doubts the commissioner will answer his voicemail.

Peyton, Eli Manning assemble star-studded crew for 'ManningCast: Heist'

That leaves the brothers with another option: infiltrate NFL headquarters and hack its computer system to change their schedule. The Mannings recruit an all-star crew that includes Hathaway, Serena Williams and Houston Texans coach DeMeco Ryans.

Peyton told Hooks that the concept came from the brothers' childhood interest in movies and their desire to top previous schedule reveals such as "ManningCast Auditions" and "ManningCast: The Musical."

"When we weren't playing football growing up, we were watching movies," Peyton said. "It's essentially our homage to the heist and action movies we grew up watching."

The star power extends well beyond Hathaway, Rudd, Powell, Hamm and David. Jason and Travis Kelce appear in the short, while the NFL contingent includes Goodell, Sean McVay, Mike McDaniel, Ryans and other current and former players and coaches.

Horowitz told Weprin that Omaha's elaborate projects surrounding the ManningCast have helped attract prominent entertainers to the show.

"I think part of the reason that Paul Rudd, Kevin Hart, or David Letterman appears on the Manningcast is because we do things like this," Horowitz said. "If the Manningcast was just a football show, Peyton and Eli probably could still recruit lots of great people."

The sixth season will culminate with another milestone for Peyton and Eli. The brothers told Hooks they will broadcast their first Super Bowl ManningCast when Super Bowl LXI takes place in Los Angeles , adding another major event to Omaha Productions' expanding version of the alternate broadcast.

articles.summary: Davion Mitchell could be one of the most impactful players on the Heat roster.
articles.body:
With the arrivals of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson, the Miami Heat are definitely in a new era. They are ready to compete for the championship again as they want to build on the foundation of those two players and Bam Adebayo.

Of course, the attention is on the big names in Miami, but there are some players who might not get the attention that they deserve. The biggest X-factor for the Heat could be Davion Mitchell, who is most likely the starting point guard in Erik Spoelstra's system moving forward.

Gabe Vincent sees Davion Mitchell as one of the Heat's most important players

For most of his career, Mitchell has been exclusively known as a defensive stopper. Over the years, Mitchell has gradually improved his game as an offensive player as well because he has upped his scoring and playmaking.

During the 2025-26 season, Mitchell started all 70 games he played, averaging 9.3 points, 6.5 assists, and a steal per game. Those are some impressive numbers, but it could get even better with the new-look Heat.

Playing alongside Antetokounmpo and Thompson could help unlock Mitchell even more. He will have the ball in his hands often, but he could also benefit from his new teammates' gravity by becoming a better shooter.

In the 2025-26 season, he averaged 39.5% from beyond the arc. This three-point shooting could become key because the Heat desperately need floor spacing outside of Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. Former Heat guard Gabe Vincent definitely thinks Mitchell is the key.

"It's going to be Giannis, and then Klay setting the screens. Then Davion becomes your X factor. He becomes your X factor entirely. If Davion isn't making three 3s a game, it's going to look very different," Vincent said about Mitchell's role on the Heat in a conversation with Trey Mourning .

The Heat have a good chance of becoming one of the Eastern Conference's best teams. Of course, they will have to work hard to beat the other top squads like the defending champions, the New York Knicks and the LeBron James-led Philadelphia 76ers .

articles.body:
Along with the rest of the team, the Oregon Ducks defense got off to a slow start in their season-opening victory over the Boise State Broncos .

The Broncos received the opening kickoff and marched down the field, completing an 11-play, 75-yard drive with a 13-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Maddux Madsen. There was little resistance from the Oregon defense, as Boise State had success both on the ground and through the air.

By the time the second half rolled around, the Ducks began to put the clamps on the Broncos offense. While the effort as a whole wasn't good enough, with Boise State putting 27 points on the board, the yardage outputs were solid from a defensive perspective: 181 passing yards and 93 rush yards for 274 total yards.

If the Ducks give up those amounts of yards, they're going to win a very high percentage of games. Yet, with the difference in talent level on the field and how high of a standard head coach Dan Lanning holds for this defense, it simply wasn't good enough.

While there's much to fix and improve upon, here's where the Ducks' defense and special teams land in various stat categories through one game.

articles.title: A familiar foe awaits Christian Gonzalez in the Patriots’ opener
articles.summary: It will be a rematch between Christian Gonzalez and Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Wednesday's NFL opener between the Patriots and Seahawks.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. – There has been a lot of focus on Christian Gonzalez's status for the New England Patriots' season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. Would he agree to a contract extension with the Patriots , and if not, would he be willing to play without a new deal in place?

The Patriots staved off those concerns by agreeing to a four-year, $135 million deal with the star cornerback on early Tuesday. And with that, the timing lines up perfectly for Wednesday's rematch with Seahawks All-Pro wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

The Seahawks have one of the best wide receivers in the league, and it will likely be Gonzalez's job to cover him. On Monday, the fourth-year defender was very complimentary of Smith-Njigba.

"Jaxon's a great, great receiver," Gonzalez told reporters. "I respect him completely. I mean, he can do it all. Everybody saw the year he had last year, and just being from the same area, it's real cool to watch each other come up and then be able to play on the biggest stage and support each other and see each other do what we do. So, it's fun."

Last season, Smith-Njigba was named the 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year and earned the First-team All-Pro honor.

"Well, just the suddenness, route craft. He is smooth, he can play at different speeds, he plays inside, he runs a full route tree, he is strong at the catch point," Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr explained. "But I just think that the savviness and the ability to get in and out of breaks is really impressive."

However, in the Super Bowl, Smith-Njigba wasn't as big a factor as he had been in past games, with Gonzalez holding him to just four receptions for 27 yards. The Patriots are going to need that again from the cornerback as they look to get revenge and start the season with a win over the reigning Super Bowl champions.

articles.title: Erislandy Lara vs Tim Tszyu in the works for December
articles.summary: Tim Tszyu’s first middleweight title shot could land on home soil this winter against ageless wonder Erislandy Lara
articles.body:
George Rose of No Limit Boxing tells Fox Sports Australia that "negotiations [are] close to being finalised" for a December clash between WBA middleweight champion Erislandy Lara and former super welterweight titlist Tim Tszyu in Australia.

Lara (32-3-3, 19 KO), 43 years old and a full 15 years removed from his infamous robbery loss to Paul Williams, stands as arguably the top middleweight in the game following Janibek Alimkhanuly's departure for greener and slightly heavier pastures. That said, he's been short on top competition since his grueling 2019 draw with Brian Castano; his current seven-fight winning streak features such titans as Spike O'Sullivan, Michael Zerafa, and the husk of Danny Garcia.

To be clear, this isn't entirely his fault. He was days away from fighting Alimkhanuly in a three-weight unification last December before "Qazaq Style" failed a drug test . There won't be nearly as much hardware involved here, but it'll be his highest-profile fight of the 2020s and should be correspondingly lucrative.

Tszyu (28-3, 18 KO), 12 years his junior, seems to have put his nightmare skid behind him with three straight wins of his own. The most recent of them saw him grind down former welterweight stud Errol Spence Jr , proving his unc-slaying chops in the process.

Honestly, I like it. It's one of the more interesting fights this choking sea turtle of a division can offer, especially with Lara's legs too weathered to stink out the joint like in his heyday. Could be fun.

articles.title: Jacob Sexton injury update: Oklahoma State football OL out for season with leg injury
articles.summary: Oklahoma State football lineman Jacob Sexton injured his leg in Tulsa loss and will miss the rest of the season.
articles.body:
STILLWATER — Oklahoma State starting left tackle Jacob Sexton is out for the season with a lower right leg injury , coach Eric Morris said Tuesday.

OSU's depth chart entering Saturday's game against No. 2 Oregon (11 a.m., ESPN) lists junior Desmond Magiya or sophomore Shaun Torgeson at left tackle. Against Tulsa, Magiya was the first to replace Sexton at left tackle while Torgeson and senior Ashton Lepo took turns also.

Sexton, senior left tackle, injured his right leg on OSU's first offensive series of the season. Playing at Oklahoma last year, Sexton suffered a season-ending injury in the first game.

"Heart goes out to Jacob, a guy who has definitely been our best offensive lineman since we've been here," Morris said Saturday. "Somebody that's worked so hard this offseason to get himself back into shape. He's been plagued by injuries his whole entire career."

Morris said after the Tulsa game he will watch the film and grade his replacement options along the line.

"I didn't think we had a great answer on the edge," Morris said. "(Magiya) got beat a number of times around the edge, got a holding penalty at a crucial time in the game. So I think Sexton, obviously you lose a really good player at left tackle, that's not what you want but that's not an excuse. They took it to us in so many different areas."

articles.title: A look back through the series history between the Saints and Lions
articles.summary: As the Saints prepare to start their 2026 season at the Lions, here's a look back through the series history between these teams.
articles.body:
Wins and losses count again when the New Orleans Saints play at the Detroit Lions on Sunday in the 2026 season opener.

The Saints are coming off a 1-2 preseason and are expected to be much improved over their 6-11 finish from a year ago. Host Detroit was 2-1 in the preseason. The Lions finished 9-8 in 2025, their fourth straight winning record, but missed the playoffs for the first time since the 2022 campaign.

New Orleans and Detroit meet for the 29th overall time on Sunday. It's the first time they've clashed since the 2023 season and the first time the Saints have played in Detroit since 2020. Here's a look at the series history between these squads.

New Orleans Saints at Dallas Cowboys: Best photos of preseason Week 3

Longest winning streak: 4 (Saints; 2008-12)

Last meeting in Detroit (2020): Saints 35-29

Between 2008 and 2017, the Saints and Lions played eight times in a 10-year span. New Orleans won five of those matchups, including a 45-28 victory during a 2011 wild-card matchup in the Superdome. That has been the only postseason matchup between these teams. In the eight years between 2018 and 2025, New Orleans and Detroit would face just twice with each squad winning in the home stadium of the other.

New Orleans and Detroit have played each other seven times in September. The Saints own a 4-3 edge against the Lions in September matchups. Three of those were in Detroit. New Orleans won only one of those, a 22-14 victory in the Silverdome in 1988.

The Saints and Lions have opened their regular season against each other twice before this coming year. In 2000, Detroit came into the Superdome and emerged with a 14-10 victory. The Saints again hosted the Lions to begin their 2009 season, one that ended with a Super Bowl XLIV championship. This time, New Orleans came away with a resounding 45-27 win.

articles.title: Retired UFC legend arrested for drunk driving
articles.summary: Ex-UFC fighter Diego Sanchez was arrested and detained on suspicions of drunk driving
articles.body:
Retired UFC fighter Diego Sanchez spent the night in jail after he was arrested on drunk driving charges in Soccoro County, N.M., on Monday.

Online court records show that Sanchez was taken into custody and charged with aggravated driving under the influence (blood alcohol level greater than .16). He was also charged with a probation violation.

KOB4 in New Mexico first reported the arrest.

It was just in February that Sanchez struck a plea deal with prosecutors in Albuquerque, N.M. after he was arrested in 2025 on multiple gun charges. As part of his plea deal, Sanchez pled guilty to a charge of shooting at or from a motor vehicle with no great bodily harm, which is classified as a fourth-degree felony

Sanchez was ultimately handed a sentence of five years of supervised probation as a result.

Part of the condition of his probation is that Sanchez was ordered to stay away from alcohol so this latest arrest could potentially trigger a whole new set of problems for the veteran fighter.

As of now, no bond has been set for Sanchez's release and he remains in lockup in Soccoro County Jail.

articles.title: Referees Have Nothing To Hide. The NFL and NCAA Should Show Every Big Replay Review Live on TV.
articles.summary: Plus: The NBA’s punishments to Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers are great, but not quite enough; and an ode to the friendships connected by fantasy football
articles.body:
Hello and welcome to another edition of Free Agent ! It's a great week to do something old-fashioned .

Many thanks to my colleague Eric Boehm for doing a great job with the newsletter last week while I was on vacation. This week, let's talk about everyone's favorite thing to complain about: referees. Then we'll have a last word on the Kawhi Leonard salary cap circumvention scandal, followed by a brief ode to fantasy football.

Speaking of which, it's not fantasy football, but you can join our NFL Survivor group on ESPN. Click here to join , and if it asks you for a password, it's "freemindsmarkets" without the quotation marks. It's free to play, and your prize is a shoutout in the newsletter. Best of luck to defending champ Primetime Paulie Rothrock, who kept his streak going through 13 games last season.

The White House put out its own version of the famous Big Ten "Maps" commercial . I want to hate it, but the song is so catchy that it's hard to hate anything while you're listening to it.

This does not bode well for the congressional efforts to regulate the NCAA and college sports: The House of Representatives is canceling two weeks of session.

The huge UMass upset of Rutgers has New Jersey Republicans angry about the $5 million in taxpayer funds that was supposed to help Rutgers build a better football team.

Pickleball is no longer the fastest-growing sport in the country: It's padel (which is basically the same).

Awkward: A developer hoping to bring the NHL back to Atlanta had to clarify the potential team's status after a positive-sounding statement was rebuffed by the NHL saying an Atlanta expansion team is "not even remotely close to an application phase."

A monthly reminder that sometimes fans can bully owners or leagues into doing what fans want: Ken Rosenthal said "the negative environment" at Los Angeles Angels games had an impact on owner Arte Moreno selling the team.

When you have a tweet go somewhat viral, you get to pick yourself for tweet of the week:

The NFL and College Football Need To Embrace Replay Review Transparency

In the wake of feeble Michigan's controversial Hail-Mary win over Western Michigan , I am not here to jump on the bandwagon calling the game rigged. But the bandwagon saying so is still a problem for college football—and the NFL. The Big Ten should not just release a statement and some video and move on.

The NCAA and NFL should make real refereeing transparency the norm, and always give TV broadcasts access to referee audio during replay reviews.

This is already the standard in ACC games. Just check out this review from a Clemson-Georgia Tech game last year.

You could argue that review took a little too much time, but the referees eventually got the call right, and everyone watching live on TV knew exactly why they decided what they decided.

About two hours after the Michigan game, the Big Ten finally released a statement on the ending, including audio of the referee discussion and video of what they were looking at.

That statement included a lackluster explanation of why the broadcast and stadium clocks seemed to be different from the clock used on the replay system. The delayed explanation of what happened allowed for two hours of people on social media calling the game rigged .

Sure, some cranks still would have called the game rigged if the Big Ten had done the right thing and aired audio and video of the review as it happened. But calling the game rigged would have been a conspiracy theory instead of a mainstream opinion.

Legitimacy is so important to sports. Sure, some people like the preordained theatrics of professional wrestling. But fans want to believe in total authenticity—that referees are completely neutral arbiters with no bias or corruption. Any doubt in the result can hinder fan engagement.

(Can confirm the time I was closest to quitting the NFL was after the Lions were brutally and repeatedly robbed by crap officiating during a primetime game against the Packers—naturally I went to a Lions game a month later).

There's no reason for referees or leagues to be wary of airing replay review discussions live. The ACC is doing it. The Big Ten is already going to do it for some Friday night games —why not all? The United Football League has done this for years , and sometimes even lets broadcasters interview the official who made the call. The NFL should set the standard for refereeing transparency and air replay review discussions live as soon as possible.

The NBA's Clippers Punishment Is Great—But Not Great Enough

The NBA's punishments of Kawhi Leonard and Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer for salary cap circumvention are right and just. But there are a few problems with the penalties.

In case you, too, were on vacation last week, the NBA announced on Wednesday that everyone involved in the scandal had broken league rules . The Clippers are losing five first-round draft picks, from 2029 through 2033 (some trades already affected the 2027 and 2028 picks). The team is fined $30 million, and Leonard is fined $700,000. Ballmer is banned from league and team activities for a year. Leonard's business manager, "Uncle Dennis" Robertson, is banned from doing any NBA business for five years. Other executives are punished as well, and the team will be "subject to a compliance and monitoring program overseen by the league office" for five years.

Those penalties are harsh and well-deserved. It seemed obvious since the scandal broke that Ballmer and Leonard were guilty . But here are a few problems.

Even without the first-round picks, the Clippers can still field a great team. Since the NBA has a soft salary cap (i.e., teams pay a "tax" to other teams and the league when payroll gets over a certain level), there's nothing stopping the Clippers— except the Clippers themselves —from spending hundreds of millions of dollars on salary and still fielding a high-quality team without those draft picks. I would have liked a punishment where the Clippers weren't allowed to spend over a certain amount on payroll for a set period of time, but a punishment like that doesn't seem to be an option for the league under the collective bargaining agreement . Also, are we sure the Clippers would actually follow these payroll limits?

The other problem is that, despite being a harsh punishment that would have owners think twice about breaking the rules, the NBA so far doesn't appear to be actually doing anything to catch future rulebreakers who do what Leonard and Ballmer did. Is the plan to just rely on the crack team at Pablo Torre Finds Out to find every salary cap circumventer, or is the league going to change its processes and transparency standards?

Lastly, Leonard actually got off relatively easy. He earned perhaps $50 million or more from these inappropriate, no-show endorsement deals—but his only punishment is paying back $700,000 in fines. From the players' side of things, that doesn't seem like a huge deterrence.

Regardless, I feel sorry for Clippers fans. The fans didn't do anything wrong, and since Leonard joined the team all the fans have to celebrate is just one conference finals appearance. Now there's a cloud of corruption over the team as long as Leonard and Ballmer are involved—as there should be.

Let's close with a brief shoutout to fantasy football—keeping friends together with good-natured ribbing for over two decades.

There are probably at least 10 friends I'd have lost touch with if it weren't for weekly interactions through my various fantasy football or pick'em leagues. Several more friends I wouldn't have met at all. I rarely see these people in person, but I'm still excited whenever I hear news about their weddings, babies, new jobs, etc.

Technically, this is all a form of sports betting—but that's pretty much an afterthought. The point is doing it with your friends, not randoms. How else are you going to spend two years mocking the guy who drafted Kyle Pitts one time? (It was one time!)

After all that clock drama, we certainly can't go with the Michigan Hail Mary—so here's some amazing defense in the clutch (with an honorable mention to one of the best punts I've ever seen).

That's all for this week. Enjoy watching the real games of the week. Who needs the NFL in Australia when you can watch the Australian Football League semifinals , and the rest of their playoffs, for $72 ?

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers did not expect Steelers to keep four QBs
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers was surprised to see every quarterback make the roster.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers entered the preseason with one of the most talked-about quarterback rooms in the NFL. With Mason Rudolph as the veteran backup, second-year quarterback Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar were both looking to show that they could be the future of the team at the position throughout the summer.

Many believed that Howard would take over for Rudolph as the No. 2 quarterback, as long as he played well enough in training camp and preseason to give Pittsburgh enough confidence to make that decision, while Allar would be the high-ceiling "project" quarterback for Mike McCarthy to try and mold into a potential starter. Rather than moving on from Rudolph and keeping both young signal callers, Pittsburgh kept all four – something Rodgers himself did not expect.

"I did not expect four quarterbacks on the roster," Rodgers said on Cam Heyward's podcast, Not Just Football . "I've never been part of [a room that kept] four quarterbacks. There were many years where two were just active and one on the p-squad. I knew when Drew was picked that would definitely shake things up in that room…"

Rodgers applauded Rudolph for his improvement during the offseason, as well as his play in the first preseason game agains the Green Bay Packers, saying he "closed the door" on the backup quarterback conversation. He also noted how proud he was of both Howard and Allar.

"I was proud of both those guys," Rodgers said. "I love Will. He's been in my hip pocket for a year now… it was fun to see him go out there because he's basically a rookie. He didn't play last year in the preseason… and Drew's been a sponge, as well. Quiet, as most rookies are. But it's one of my all-time favorite rooms for sure."

Part II of Heyward and Rodgers' conversation comes out later this week.

The sixth-seeded Czech reached her first US Open quarterfinal by beating Marta Kostyuk 7-5, 5-7, 6-4 on Sunday. Brad Gilbert, Coco Gauff’s former coach, also picked Noskova as a player others should be watching, adding weight to her growing run in New York at this stage too.Brad Gilbert’s Linda Noskova warning puts Aryna Sabalenka on alertGilbert made his view clear while discussing the US Open with Ajla Tomljanovic. “I was thinking about this morning; we have barely mentioned and she’s under the radar… If she wins this tournament, she’s the best player in 26. Linda Noskova,” he said, according to Yardbarker.There is a reason that prediction stands out. Noskova is the reigning Wimbledon champion, and she has already shown that she can stay in a match after things start going badly. Against Kostyuk, she led 7-5, 5-3 and had two match points, only for the Ukrainian to save both and force a third set. Noskova recovered and closed the match on her sixth match point.The win also ended a long wait for Noskova at Flushing Meadows. Before this tournament, her best US Open result was the third round. She has now beaten Katie Volynets, Lanlana Tararudee, Ann Li and Kostyuk to reach the last eight. The US Open also notes that this is her first quarterfinal at the tournament.Her Wimbledon title gives the run more meaning. Noskova beat Karolína Muchová 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in the final after failing to convert five championship points in the second set. She then reset herself and won the deciding set. That experience matters now because her next opponent is a player who has been extremely hard to stop in New York.Her hard-court results before New York were mixed, which makes this run harder to predict. The US Open reported that her best hard-court result of the season before the tournament was the Indian Wells semifinals, while she lost in the second round in Toronto and fourth round in Cincinnati. That makes this run unexpected.Linda Noskova’s US Open path after Marta Kostyuk winAryna Sabalenka is waiting in the quarterfinals on Tuesday. The world No. 1 has not lost a set at this US Open and owns a 2-0 record against Noskova. Their latest meeting came in the Indian Wells semifinals in March, when Sabalenka won 6-3, 6-4.Still, Noskova is not entering the match without confidence. The US Open said she expects “some fast tennis” and knows Sabalenka’s serve and baseline game will be the main challenge. Noskova’s own game is built around hard hitting from the baseline, so this could come down to who handles the big points better.If Noskova beats Sabalenka, the semifinal would be against the winner of Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro. On the other side of the draw, Coco Gauff, Iga Swiatek, Elena Rybakina and Naomi Osaka are among the players who could still reach the final.For now, though, Noskova only has to deal with Sabalenka. She has already survived one difficult three-set battle. The bigger question is whether she can repeat that level against the defending champion.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Klay Kubiak discusses the 49ers left guard competition and who will play
articles.summary: The 49ers will have multiple bodies active on game day capable of playing left guard
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak addressed the media, where he spoke about what's going on at left guard. Kubiak acknowledged the "very difficult challenge" it takes to prepare for Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, but said the players on the other side of the ball won't determine which player plays:

"I don't think so. I think you play who you feel most comfortable with. I think I said this a few weeks ago, though; it's like, when you look at guard, there's never any reason why guys can't rotate as well. I mean, multiple guys can play in the game, and we'll see how the game goes with who we start and kind of how we want to do the rotation.

But you've got to get a feel for how the game's going and how guys are handling stuff. So, nothing's settled, nothing's determined right now. It's not going to be based on experience necessarily. We're going to go with who we think should start based on who's had the best camp and kind of where they're at, and see how the game goes."

Kubiak said he didn't know if the 49ers would rotate players during the game, saying, "We're going to have multiple guys up and multiple guys ready to go. So, whether they rotate or not, that'll be determined as the game goes."

The options include Carver Willis, Connor Colby, and maybe Jarrett Patterson. Realistically, Patterson is Jake Brendel's backup, and Colby rotates if Willis looks like he's being overwhelmed.

It's not an easy situation if you're the 49ers. Whether it's Willis or Colby, they're both inexperienced and need to learn on the fly. When you haven't played, mistakes are inevitable. The team can help Willis out by sliding protections a specific way or putting more on Brendel's plate, so Willis is the lineman who is free in obvious passing situations.

But there's only so much you can do to hide your left guard. For the most part, he's going to have to play and hold his own in 1-on-1 situations. Willis and Colby are above-average athletes. Any perceived struggles won't happen when they're on the move. Where they might find themselves in trouble his holding up against power or length.

We'll find out in a little more than 48 hours if Willis is up to the task or if the Niners are content with playing musical chairs at left guard once again.

articles.title: A very smart list of Vanoli’s top five priorities
articles.summary: The new mister’s got his work cut out for him.
articles.body:
The Fabio Grosso era is over after 3 games, 3 losses, 9 goals conceded, and 1 scored. Paolo Vanoli is back in the saddle and trying to herd the Viola back into shape. Much like last year, he's got a lot to do. Fortunately, he doesn't have to worry about European games taking up his training sessions and sapping his players' energy. Instead, he can focus on fixing what's broken in this team. Even with that extra time, though, he'll have to focus on a few specific areas of improvement. As far as I can tell, here are the top five.

This is the most obvious issue and I swear the other four are more concrete. The simple fact is, though, that Grosso's team never seemed sure of what it was doing. I think that's a matter of communication more than tactical acumen. For example, he repeatedly stated that Moise Kean wasn't central to his plans in press conferences, which contributed to the striker's eventual animosity towards Fiorentina. Alienating the best player is about as bad a way to introduce yourself to a team as exists.

On the field, though, Grosso's players seemed deeply disorganized. The passivity out of possession might've been a tactical choice but it often felt like nobody was sure what the pressing triggers were and thus stayed in the shape at all times. It was risk aversion projected and distorted to a gargantuan parody of itself. Going forward, things were just as disjointed. Aside from a few tidy combinations down the left, every move began with a hopeful thump up to the striker and continued with a lucky bounce. It was all too reliant on individuals doing stuff. Even a team built on winning 1-v-1 battles needs some structure and Grosso couldn't provide it anything beyond, "Don't make a mistake."

Vanoli's job isn't necessarily to install the complex, repeatable mechanisms of his old master Antonio Conte. What he needs to do, though, is explain to every player what exactly it is that they do around here. Nobody can do their job when they don't know what their job is and Paolo Vanoli isn't shy about telling people what their jobs are. He expects his players to fulfill their roles and he'll bench anyone who doesn't. Making sure that every individual knows their role and the overarching design of the team is priority number one.

Fabio Paratici built this Fiorentina to attack directly and quickly, getting bodies forward en masse to overwhelm opponents. Grosso leaned into it, giving two of three central midfielders and both fullbacks license to break, which in turn left the team understaffed at the back. When opponents counterattacked, the pitch opened up to them like a sunny highway with barely an obstacle in sight. Think of Paulo Dybala picking up the ball near midfield and motoring into the final third unopposed to play in Donyell Malen three different times if you want an illustrative example. Frosinone and Torino offered their own variations on the theme as well. It was disastrous.

By now, most people have heard the term "rest defense." Fiorentina didn't have one. Too often, opponents attacked just 3 players: 2 centerbacks and a midfielder in front of them. These are the situations that amplify any defensive mistake and make players look slow or dumb or clownish. The simple fact is that very few players can routinely snuff out attackers running at pace. The pitch is too big, the opponents are too talented. Guys who can routinely do that snuffing don't tend to hang around Florence for long. When the talent doesn't offer solutions, coaches turn to tactics.

There are a couple of obvious solutions. The first is keeping one of the midfielders deeper. Adding 33% more bodies to break up counters helps a lot. Marco Brescianini and Cher Ndour are at their best breaking into the opposing penalty area but might need to sacrifice for the good of the team, staying home and using their physicality to protect rather than provoke. Keeping at least one fullback lower would also offer more protection. Fiorentina doesn't have the talent to attack with just three or four and score goals so Vanoli needs to find a balance. Grosso tipped it way too far one way and the new mister has to slide it back.

I've been hammering on this since the summer friendlies and it drove me crazy. Fiorentina's defense was way too narrow at all times. Grosso's priority seemed to be defending the gap between fullback and centerback at all costs. That makes some sense: a ball slipped into that channel often results in a shot or a cutback. He went all out to prevent that, though, to the point that it undermined his defensive structure completely because, as the fullbacks collapsed in, they left the opposing wingers/wingbacks in space. So much space. So. Much. Space.

Benevento cottoned on pretty quickly and created some danger by hitting long diagonals to the wide areas. Roma, Frosinone, and Torino took notes and exploited the same glaring weakness. All they had to do was keep someone high and wide and switch the play to them. Serie A forwards are good enough to bring the ball down and build up a head of steam while driving at a static defender, which makes it easy to go past them. Time and again, opponents hit that pass and profited.

I understand Grosso's reasoning. His rightbacks are all shaky defensively. Víctor Valdepeñas on the left is a converted centerback and isn't used to defending the wide areas. By sticking to the same approach even after the players demonstrated that it didn't suit them, Grosso doomed them to structural hell. Even a shaky defender has a better chance of stopping a skillful winger on the initial pass than when that winger's had time to settle the ball and generate momentum. Valdepeñas misjudged that high switch a dozen times in these first games; the last example was Torino's winner.

I expect Vanoli will widen his defense, accepting a bit more room in the channels at the expense of sticking closer to the wingers. Keeping another midfielder deeper could help as well since the regista won't be solely responsible for shielding openings on both sides of the pitch. Paradoxically, aggressive pressing higher up could help as well: if opponents don't have time and space to pick that diagonal pass, it's no longer a threat. Grosso's insistence on risk aversion above all else paradoxically put his defense at greater risk than anything else he did. Vanoli should be bolder if he wants more security.

Fiorentina's only good passer in deep positions is Fagioli. The other midfielders are all ball-carriers rather than playmakers. The fullback are likewise dribblers and overlappers. Of the centerbacks, only Marin Pongračić has shown the ability to break the lines and even that ability comes and goes. Opponents know that if they can take Nicky Beans out of the game, they can render Fiorentina entirely one-dimensional, reliant on long balls out the back. Mateo Pellegrino's a decent hold-up striker but not good enough to be the only outlet, especially since David de Gea and his defense aren't exactly pinpoint distributors.

With such limitations, there's only so much Grosso could've done. Deep buildup, however, is also the most structured part of the in-possession side of the game, which gives the coach more control over that phase than any other. Grosso was unwilling or unable to create a structure that 1) concealed or minimized his players' weaknesses as passers and 2) offered multiple solutions to getting out of his own third.

Vanoli's got a leg up here because he dealt with this same problem last year. He didn't solve it but he figured out how to coexist with it. For my money, the solution is dropping another player or two into the deep areas. This provides more angles for out balls and more simple passes that won't tax limited players as heavily. If the opponent sends another marker to follow those extra deep options, it opens space higher up so that the eventual long ball has a better chance of reaching a Fiorentina forward, who then has fewer obstacles between himself and the goal.

The other obvious solution is Dodô, who's been the answer to this question for years. His ability to burst past a defender allows Fiorentina to move itself out of danger. Even if he only dribbles to midfield before dumping the ball off to a teammate, opponents will scramble back into their defensive shape and stop pressing as hard because the risk/reward balance chances the farther from goal you get. I don't think João Mário or Valepeñas can reliably beat a defender in deep positions as consistently so Dodô might be back in the XI for the foreseeable.

Last year, Fiorentina was the worst team in Serie A at defending set pieces. The inability to defend corners and free kicks was a weekly fixture in the What We Learned section of every match report. Paratici obviously identified that as an area that he could improve pretty easily by bringing in a bunch of tall and strong players. I'm halfway convinced that Radu Drǎgușin's really only here to get his noggin on dead balls rather than defend in open play. I expected massive improvement in this department under Grosso.

And you know what? Grosso and his set piece coach Giuseppe Foti did just that. Fiorentina hasn't conceded a set piece goal this season and has mostly defended those situations fairly well, although Frosinone did cause some problems. No, my beef with Grosso in this regard is that Fiorentina's attacking set pieces were almost hilariously bad. Their primary feature was Franco Mastantuono putting in a low ball that hit the first defender in the midsection, allowing opponents to break the other way with the Viola all out of sorts.

I don't share the Proper Football Man disdain for targeting the front post at corners. Sure, when that first defender clears the ball, it looks bad. But making first contact means putting the opposing defense under a ton of pressure, as we've seen this year: look at Drǎgușin's assist for back post demon Luca Ranieri against Benevento. Sure, you have to consider the opposition, but it works. Adding a bunch of burly dudes should only increase Fiorentina's options and danger from dead balls.

Vanoli's ambivalence about set pieces last year was notable. He explained after his first game that they weren't something he'd had time to train and it seemed like he never prioritized them, at least if the team's hopelessness at ever corner and free kick was any indication. He's got much better tools this time around, though, and needs to use them. Set piece goals have never been a greater point of emphasis and the new mister will struggle to turn things around if his team ends up at a net deficit from those situations.

For now, the Seahawks enter Week 1 viewed as one of the NFL's premier teams.

articles.title: Big 12 steps up in Week 2 with seven matchups against the Big Ten, SEC and ACC
articles.summary: Kansas coach Lance Leipold saw enough of Missouri playing on television the night before his Jayhawks opened their own season with a romp over lower-level Lo...
articles.body:
LAWRENCE, Kan. (AP) — Kansas coach Lance Leipold saw enough of Missouri playing on television the night before his Jayhawks opened their own season with a romp over lower-level Long Island University that he could confidently deliver an obvious message to his team afterward.

"We know," Leipold said, "it's going to be a lot different test Friday night."

That's because the Tigers were just as impressive in rolling past Arkansas-Pine Bluff in their season opener.

Indeed, the latest edition of the Border War between former Big 12 rivals Kansas and Missouri is one of several high-profile matchups involving the league this weekend. And in almost every case, they are games that will represent a big step up in the level of competition after the majority of the Big 12 put up some gaudy Week 1 numbers in lopsided blowouts over inferior opponents.

The Jayhawks rolled to a 51-6 win over the Sharks . Down the road, Kansas State blew out Nicholls 71-3 in the debut of new coach Collin Klein. Arizona State and UCF also hit the 70-point mark in wins over Morgan State and Bethune-Cookman, respectively, giving the Big 12 three of the five Football Bowl Subdivision teams to reach that barrier last week.

Good luck coming close to that prolific offensive output this weekend.

The Jayhawks lost to the Tigers last season in lopsided fashion, and Missouri just might be even better this year. The Wildcats step up to play Washington State, which had Washington on the ropes . Arizona State plays Texas A&M while UCF has Pittsburgh.

Elsewhere, Utah moves on from its 66-14 blowout of Idaho to play Arkansas in another Big 12-SEC showdown. Iowa State, which put away Southeast Missouri State, prepares for its biggest rival in Iowa. Texas Tech goes from Abilene to Oregon State in the second week of the season, and Oklahoma State — still smarting from a loss to Tulsa — has to deal with Oregon now.

"It's really easy to lead when things are going well and good," first-year Cowboys coach Eric Morris said. "It's hard to lead when things aren't going well, and you get punched in the mouth like that. It's on me to get us back collectively and regroup."

It's critical not just for Oklahoma State but for the league in general.

The depth and strength of the Big Ten and SEC give those power conferences a big advantage when it comes to qualifying teams for the 12-team College Football Playoff. Of the seven at-large bids handed out by the selection committee last year, none went to the Big 12, leaving only conference champion Texas Tech to fly the flag on behalf of the league.

The SEC had four at-large picks, the Big Ten had two and the Atlantic Coast Conference had the remaining choice in Miami.

In other words, weekends like this coming one are of paramount importance for the Big 12, giving the league a chance to flex its own muscles with seven head-to-head matchups against its power conference brethren. And they are even more important given the Big 12 has already lost two such games: North Carolina beat TCU and Auburn beat Baylor.

The league's coaches know what's at stake, too. It's why Leipold was so quick to move from a lopsided win over Long Island right into Missouri, and UCF coach Scott Frost had a message for his team — with Pittsburgh on deck — after beating Bethune-Cookman.

"You know, I told the team after the game, we can't go patting ourselves on the back for this. This is just what they're supposed to do," Frost said. "We have a really big test next week."

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s sharp cricket brain shines! 15-year-old plots two big wickets in Duleep Trophy final – Watch
articles.summary: In the Duleep Trophy final, young talent Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, only 15, demonstrated remarkable tactical skills that greatly benefitted the East Zone team. H...
articles.body:
NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may only be 15, but the teenage sensation is already showing the tactical awareness of a seasoned cricketer. The East Zone vice-captain played a key role in two crucial dismissals as his side tightened the screws on South Zone in the Duleep Trophy final at the MA Chidambaram Stadium. After East Zone piled up a mammoth 708, largely courtesy of captain Ishan Kishan's magnificent 270, South Zone appeared to be settling into their reply. But Sooryavanshi's sharp reading of the game helped East Zone strike twice before tea on Day 3.

Sooryavanshi trusts his instinct for crucial DRS call

The first breakthrough came when Ricky Bhui appeared to have survived a caught-behind appeal against Mukesh Kumar. The pacer zipped one down the leg side as Bhui attempted to guide it away, but the on-field umpire remained unmoved despite the appeal. Sooryavanshi, however, was convinced there was something behind it. The teenager urged Kishan to take the Decision Review System (DRS), and his instinct proved spot on. UltraEdge showed a spike as the ball passed the bat, with wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra completing the catch to send Bhui back. BCCI also highlighted Sooryavanshi's intervention on social media. "Take it... take it. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi urges the captain to take the review, and it turns out to be successful," BCCI wrote, while sharing the video of the dismissal on X. It was another example of the youngster's growing influence in senior cricket. His ability to make the call under pressure was particularly impressive.

Teenage vice-captain brings Shami back at the perfect time

Sooryavanshi's tactical contribution did not end with the DRS call. With South Zone at 174/4 and only minutes remaining before tea, the youngster was temporarily standing in as captain after Kishan went off the field. He decided to bring Mohammed Shami back for a short burst despite the veteran pacer having already bowled a demanding spell. Shami had earlier walked off after bowling seven overs and had bowled only twice after lunch. He had also required treatment to his neck from the physio. Yet Sooryavanshi recognised the opportunity to use the experienced seamer for a quick spell before the interval. The move paid immediate dividends. Shami dismissed Smaran Ravichandran, the highest run-scorer of the previous Ranji Trophy season, when the Karnataka batter chased a delivery outside off and nicked it behind. The on-field umpire again did not give the batter out, but this time Kushagra urged Sooryavanshi to review. UltraEdge once again confirmed the edge. Ravichandran was gone, South Zone were reduced to 176/5, and Sooryavanshi had played a direct role in two of East Zone's most important wickets.

DRS instinct becoming a Sooryavanshi trademark

The decision-making has not been a one-off for Sooryavanshi in this Duleep Trophy campaign. During East Zone's semifinal against Central Zone in Bengaluru, the youngster made another bold DRS call after Aryan Juyal was initially given not out following a caught-behind appeal against Mukesh Kumar. Juyal, batting on 46, pushed hard at a delivery outside off and the East Zone players immediately appealed. When the umpire rejected the appeal, there was some hesitation among the fielders over whether to review. Sooryavanshi trusted his instinct and called for the review at the last moment. UltraEdge detected a spike, confirming the edge and handing East Zone a crucial wicket.

The youngster had also spoken about his willingness to contribute with the ball during the tournament, joking that he considered himself a "wicket-taker". "Opponent team's wickets weren't falling, so I was asked to bowl two or three overs. Ishan Bhaiya felt like he was taking a risk, but he didn't know that I am a wicket-taker," Sooryavanshi said in a video posted by BCCI Domestic. His batting may have made him one of Indian cricket's most talked-about teenage prospects, but his Duleep Trophy campaign is increasingly showcasing another side of his game.
