articles.title: WWE's Cody Rhodes Announces Death of Dog Pharaoh in Social Media Post
articles.summary: WWE Superstar Cody Rhodes announced the death of his beloved dog, Pharaoh, on Tuesday.
articles.body:
WWE Superstar Cody Rhodes announced the death of his beloved dog, Pharaoh, on Tuesday.

Rhodes went public with the news on Instagram , sharing fond memories of his four-legged companion in the post:

A Siberian Husky, Pharaoh became a huge part of Rhodes' presentation over the years, and thus a popular figure among wrestling fans.

Pharaoh made numerous on-screen appearances during Rhodes' time in AEW from 2019 to 2022, and he was shown alongside Cody on a few occasions after he returned to WWE in 2022 as well.

Several pieces of Rhodes' merchandise incorporated Pharaoh, including T-shirts. WWE even released a plush toy and an action figure of Pharaoh.

Pharaoh's passing comes just nine months after WWE champion CM Punk announced the death of his dog, Larry.

Like Pharaoh, Larry was immortalized in T-shirt and action figure form by WWE, making them two of the most impactful pets in the history of pro wrestling.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on CM Punk, Cody Rhodes, Randy Orton, Seth Rollins and Surprise Roster Release
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

WWE's Reported Plans for Punk, Rhodes, Orton

WWE is reportedly being deliberate in its attempt to keep both Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton away from WWE champion CM Punk currently.

According to Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Wrestle Features ), the ongoing feud between Rhodes and Orton is meant to keep them occupied so that they aren't part of the WWE title scene.

However, Meltzer added that WWE has Punk vs. Rhodes and Punk vs. Orton on its radar for bigger events in the future.

Rhodes beat Orton in the main event of Night 1 of WrestleMania 42 to retain the WWE Championship, but Orton punted Rhodes after the match, only to disappear from WWE programming for the next few months.

Orton resurfaced at SummerSlam to cost Rhodes in his WWE Championship match against Punk, and Rhodes and Orton have been going at it ever since.

At Sunday Night's Main Event, Orton beat Rhodes thanks in large part to a low blow, which suggests their rivalry is likely far from over.

As for Punk, he has been dealing with plenty of potential challengers for the WWE title, beating the likes of Kevin Owens and Johnny Gargano thus far.

On this week's episode of SmackDown in Mexico, Punk is slated to put the championship on the line against Sami Zayn, who has also been a thorn in Punk's side.

There is seemingly no end in sight for Punk's title reign, which suggests future championship matches against Rhodes and Orton could indeed be in the cards for him once the Rhodes vs. Orton feud has reached its conclusion.

There is reportedly some uncertainty regarding why Seth Rollins has been off WWE programming and when he will return.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), Rollins' name has not come up backstage in WWE "in a while," and although it is believed he should "be back relatively soon," it was reportedly not the original plan for him to be gone for as long as he has been.

The Visionary was last seen on Aug. 2 when he lost to Roman Reigns in a World Heavyweight Championship match in the main event of Night 2 of SummerSlam.

Reigns and Rollins put on a classic match, and they seemed to put aside their differences in the end by doing the signature Shield fist bump as SummerSlam went off the air.

Rollins has been kept off television since then, though, perhaps because of a lack of creative plans for him coming out of SummerSlam.

He is no longer in the world heavyweight title picture, and his rivalry with The Vision came to an end before he went after Reigns as well.

Because of that, there is no clear and obvious spot for Rollins, although that could soon change with Money in the Bank coming up.

Rollins won the men's Money in the Bank ladder match last year, and he is a two-time winner of the match overall. MITB qualifiers for the Oct. 10 MITB premium live event started this week on Raw, and it won't be a shock if Rollins is included in a qualifier in the coming weeks.

A lack of progress reportedly contributed to WWE's decision to release Wendy Choo last week.

According to Meltzer (h/t Mrosko ), WWE parted ways with Choo due to the notion that she had been in NXT for years and hadn't developed to the level the company expected or hoped.

Bryan Alvarez of F4WOnline (h/t WrestlePurists ) previously reported that sources at the WWE Performance Center were "shocked" by Choo's release.

Before signing with WWE in 2019, Choo worked for multiple promotions, but her most notable stint was with Ring of Honor under the name Karen Q.

In WWE, Choo underwent numerous character changes as part of NXT. She started with an evil gimmick in the group Tian Sha, going by the name Mei Ying.

She eventually turned babyface and developed the gimmick of a wrestler who was constantly tired and wanted to nap. That character eventually took a dark, villainous turn as well.

Since last year, Choo had primarily been part of Evolve, and she ditched the over-the-top characters for one more closely resembling her real-life self.

Choo even held the Evolve Women's Championship for a couple of months before dropping it to Nikkita Lyons in May, and she had recently been wrestling in matches on Main Event.

Ultimately, WWE seemed to come to the conclusion that there was no real future for Choo on the main roster, and since she had already done all she could in NXT and Evolve, the decision was made to move on.

articles.title: Sidney Crosby Talks Next Penguins Contract, Retirement Timeline Ahead of 22nd NHL Season
articles.summary: Sidney Crosby indicated he is hoping to play multiple additional NHL seasons following his 22nd campaign with the Pittsburgh Penguins.
articles.body:
Sidney Crosby indicated he is hoping to play multiple additional NHL seasons following his 22nd campaign with the Pittsburgh Penguins.

Crosby, who is heading into his age-38 season on an expiring $8.7 million AAV deal, told reporters Tuesday his agent Pat Brisson is already discussing a new contract with Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas.

"It's just a little bit more difficult, I think, at my age, as far as trying to project where you're going to be. It's different," Crosby said (h/t the Daily Faceoff's Matt Larkin ). "You don't know where you're going to be at, kind of year, to year, how you feel, and things like that.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

"I'd like to continue playing for a number of years. I just don't know what that number is. I guess your mind and body tell you that eventually. And right now, I feel pretty good."

Crosby most recently signed a two-year contract extension ahead of the 2024-25 season. He said Tuesday whether his next deal will be a single-season or multi-year contract isn't "something that I'm set on either way," per Larkin.

About when he expected to finalize a new contract, Crosby said, per Larkin: "I wouldn't say I'm going to rush... Two summers ago, ended up getting done. So we'll see. I don't think there's a timeline on it. They're just gonna talk."

The market for top NHL centers recently exploded with the $18.8 million AAV contracts signed by the Anaheim Ducks' Leo Carlsson and San Jose Sharks' Macklin Celebrini.

Crosby has played for 18 seasons on contracts worth $8.7 million per year. He has signed at that value three times on five-year, 12-year and two-year deals, respectively.

Brisson said in a recent interview with San Jose Hockey Now's Sheng Peng Crosby's second deal was impacted by his concussion history, and that his latest extension remained at $8.7 million AAV because Crosby "didn't care much."

"He may sign a one-year deal for $12 [million]. I don't know," Brisson told Peng in July about Crosby's next deal.

Crosby averaged a point per game for a 21st straight season while leading the Penguins on their first playoff run in four years last spring.

The NHL's active points leader will be returning to Pittsburgh next season alongside longtime teammate Evgeni Malkin. Despite buzz the Penguins went into last season expecting it to be Malkin's final year in Pittsburgh, Malkin earned a one-year extension after putting up a point-per-game campaign of his own.

Whether possible trade candidates like Malkin, Rickard Rakell, Bryan Rust or Erik Karlsson are still in Pittsburgh by the March 2027 trade deadline could depend on whether Crosby is able to once more help keep his team in the playoff conversation as contract negotiations potentially continue this fall.

articles.title: MAC appeals Michigan-Western Michigan result, asks NCAA and CFP to recognize Broncos as winner
articles.summary: The Mid-American Conference appealed the outcome of the Michigan-Western Michigan game on Tuesday and asked NCAA and College Football Playoff administrators to recognize the Broncos as the actual winner.
articles.body: The Mid-American Conference appealed the outcome of the Michigan-Western Michigan game on Tuesday and asked NCAA and College Football Playoff administrators to recognize the Broncos as the actual winner. Michigan won 13-12 on a Hail Mary pass after the replay official put one second back on the clock. The stadium clock and the one shown on television showed zeroes after Bryce Underwood’s first Hail Mary was thrown out the back of the end zone. The Big Ten had said in a statement that time had not expired on a separate clock embedded within its replay system. Western Michigan and the MAC initially accepted the explanation, but that had changed by Tuesday. “After further study and investigation, it is now evident that replay protocol was not properly followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock at the conclusion of the Western Michigan vs. Michigan football game,” MAC Commissioner Jon Steinbrecher said in a statement. Messages seeking comment were sent to the NCAA and CFP. Steinbrecher said the established replay protocol requires that the game clock displayed on the program feed be used in determining whether time remained. Instead, he said, the Big Ten replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded. “This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock,” Steinbrecher said. “It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded, and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12–7.” The MAC is requesting the NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision Oversight Committee and the CFP recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations. Michigan was ranked No. 16 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll but dropped out of the rankings Tuesday.

articles.title: Spain’s FA to fund IVF, egg freezing for female football players, referees
articles.summary: Spain FA offers fertility support to female players and referees, including costs for internationals called up twice.
articles.body:
Spain’s football federation has unveiled an agreement to support fertility treatment for female players and referees, presenting the measure as another way to give women in elite football greater freedom to decide if and when to become mothers.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) said on Tuesday its agreement with the Tambre clinic would allow sportswomen to access treatments including in vitro fertilisation and egg freezing, in what the federation called a pioneering step for women’s sport in the country.

Spain internationals Olga Carmona and Patri Guijarro attended the announcement and welcomed the deal as an important tool for players managing the demands of professional sport and personal life.

“We are very happy to have reached this agreement, to have one more option to decide how and when to choose to become a mother,” Carmona said.

Guijarro said the measure formed part of a broader push to improve work-life balance for female athletes and ensure motherhood does not become a barrier to a career in elite sport.

“Ultimately, it’s a very positive agreement because it’s true that for all these years we’ve been fighting to achieve a better work-life balance for mothers,” Guijarro said.

“In the case of being able to have a career whilst being a mother, work-life balance measures are now being put in place; we feel we’ve been listened to. It’s important that female athletes feel they don’t have to choose between their professional and personal lives.”

According to Reyes Bellver Alonso, director of women’s football at the RFEF, the federation will cover the full cost of egg-freezing treatment and provide a range of benefits linked to different treatments for all international players who have been called up at least twice. The deal with Tambre will be in place until 2029.

“The debate on motherhood and work-life balance is a vast one, and it is good that these issues are being discussed because it always helps to raise their profile in other areas,” Bellver Alonso said.

She said football had made significant progress in protecting players’ rights, contracts and pregnancy safeguards, including eliminating anti-pregnancy clauses.

“If there is one area where work has been done on maternity rights, the protection of women, the protection of contracts and work-life balance in women’s sport, it is football,” she said.

“I think that we often focus on the criticism and fail to convey how beneficial and pioneering these developments are, and the struggles the players have also gone through.”

The RFEF said the agreement was not designed to discourage footballers from having children while they are active, but to offer another option so they do not have to rule out motherhood because of their sporting career.

It said the initiative complements existing work-life balance measures, including support that allows players who have become mothers to have their children close by during away trips, training camps and tournaments.

The announcement has also prompted debate among labour and equality organisations in Spain, with some warning that fertility support should not replace stronger workplace protections for mothers.

Olympic bronze medallist and triple jumper Ana Peleteiro described the measure as “deeply sexist” in a video posted on social media, while the CCOO trade union said the focus should remain on work-life balance and protecting pregnancy during competition.

articles.title: Julian Edelman: Seahawks Are 'A Storm Brewing To Wipe Out Teams'
articles.summary: Julian Edelman expressed that the Seattle Seahawks are going to "wipe out a lot of teams" this season.
articles.body: Was the 2026 NFL season just the beginning for Sam Darnold and the defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks? "I'm big on Seattle," "FOX NFL Kickoff" Analyst Julian Edelman stated on Tuesday's edition of "The Herd." "They're returning 20 of 22 starters. I got to sit and talk with all these guys in a production meeting in the preseason. Sam Darnold was mad about his performance in the Super Bowl, and the week before that he had an unbelievable game performance to beat the Los Angeles Rams. He gets to go into the offseason almost like he lost the Super Bowl with his mindset after winning a Super Bowl. And then they get to hear all the hype on the Rams. I think this is a storm brewing to just wipe out a lot of teams. They're really good. "I was so impressed with [Seahawks head coach] Mike Macdonald's calm, cool and collected demeanor but also his way where he's big with the connections with the players, but he also has kind of that hard alpha trait to him because he is a defensive guy and his mentality with steering the ship. I'm so impressed with every single guy they have." The Seahawks open the 2026 regular season at home against the Patriots on Wednesday night in a rematch of Super Bowl LX. Seattle is coming off a 14-3 season that saw it win the NFC West for the first time since 2020, with its 14 regular-season wins a franchise record and its Super Bowl triumph the second in franchise history (2013 was the first). The Seahawks lost offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, who became the new head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders, replacing him with former San Francisco 49ers offensive assistant Brian Fleury. With Darnold in his first season under center for Seattle, Kubiak's offense was third in the NFL in points (28.4 per game) and eighth in total yards (351.4 per game). Meanwhile, Seattle's defense, which returns defensive coordinator Aden Durde for a third season, was first in opponent points (17.2 per game) and sixth in total yards (285.6 per game). As for the "hype" surrounding the Rams, quarterback Matthew Stafford is coming off a 2025 campaign that saw him win NFL MVP honors. On the transactional front, Los Angeles, most notably, acquired superstar defensive end Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns and cornerback and 2023 All-Pro Trent McDuffie from the Kansas City Chiefs. And if that wasn't enough, superstar defensive lineman Aaron Donald recently came out of retirement after two years away from the game to play for the Rams once again. Seattle's offseason has primarily been based on retaining its own. The Seahawks extended wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (four-year, $168.6 million deal) and cornerback Devon Witherspoon (four-year, $132 million deal) on deals that make them the highest-paid players at their respective positions. NFL Related StoriesRams? Seahawks? Bengals? The NFL's Best Teams Heading Into Week 1Patrick Mahomes Reportedly Starting Week 1 For Chiefs Barring SetbackQB Stock Market Week 1: Projecting How All 32 Starters Will Fare In 2026Sam Darnold And The New-Look Seahawks Offense Face Huge Immediate Test Seattle also extended defensive lineman Leonard Williams (three-year, $90 million deal), while re-signing wide receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed (three-year, $51 million deal) and cornerback Josh Jobe (three-year, $24 million deal), among other moves. In the draft, the Seahawks selected Notre Dame Fighting Irish running back Jadarian Price with the No. 32 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, a pick that combats the departure of running back and Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III. "They draft, develop and pay their guys," Edelman said of the Seahawks. "They got a lot of great things going for them, and the biggest thing is that no one's even talking about them. It's the quietest Super Bowl champion team I've ever heard of. It's unreal, and it's going to play into their favor."

articles.title: Burrito-eating record smashed, Elizabeth Holmes doc trailer captivates the nation, fictional dog list debate
articles.summary: This Happy Post-Labor Tuesday Nightcaps covers Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes documentary, Leah Shutkever's burrito record, and a dog tier list.
articles.body: Happy Post-Labor Tuesday edition of Nightcaps to you, a real bittersweet day on the ol' "The Far Side" desk calendar, if ever there was one. It's the symbolic end of summer, but with that comes football (and more importantly, hockey), and what a weekend it was. But even though Summer '26 is pretty much over, I've saved one summertime ritual for September: a road trip. My wife and I (plus another passenger I will get into in a moment) will be driving from Orlando, Florida, to Pennsylvania Dutch Country to celebrate my old man retiring after 35 years of service in law enforcement. Also, there's an Iron Maiden concert nearby, but that was just a very happy coincidence. I wouldn't miss it for the world, but that doesn't mean I'm not going to still try to save a few bucks. The original plan was to fly, and it was two things: inconvenient for when we were going and expensive. 15 DOG ESSENTIALS THAT MAKE LATE-SUMMER WALKS AND ROAD TRIPS EASIER So, I convinced my wife that it would be better to drive over two days. But I also convinced her that we could save even more cheddar if we brought our French bulldog, Carl, with us. Now, the numbers check out. I stand by that. I'm also excited to give our newish Ford Bronco Sport a proper long-distance test. However, I'm starting to sweat it a little because if this road trip doesn't go off without a hitch, I will hear about it for the rest of my life. And I mean, I won't get a break from "...remember how you made us drive to Pennsylvania?" ending any semi-heated discussion until I settle into a pine box for the ol' dirt nap. I think it'll be good. I've planned it out to avoid traffic in major cities and also to make sure we're on the road so I can listen to F1 practice on the radio (don't tell my wife that part, though). Hopefully, it's entirely uneventful, and the biggest issue we encounter is a free continental breakfast somewhere in the wilds of North Carolina with a broken waffle iron. Anyway, enough about my yapping... actually, that's a lie, but we will move on to yapping about other stuff. Nathan Fielder’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary is captivating — and horrifying — to the nation. I went to see "Coyote vs. Acme" this weekend (which was great), and that meant sitting through about half an hour of trailers, ads, and Nicole Kidman waxing poetic about the magic of movies. Half an hour before a movie that was only an hour and forty minutes... Anyway, none of those trailers hold a candle to the one that dropped on Monday for awkward-moment GOAT Nathan Fielder's documentary about disgraced tech leader Elizabeth Holmes, "You Can See Everything." BOX OFFICE COMEBACK: HOW SUMMER 2026 OFFERS A GLIMMER OF HOPE FOR HOLLYWOOD IN THE POST-COVID ERA Even if you don't know what it's about, it might make your skin crawl; if you do, it will absolutely make you squirm. Holmes famously lied a lot about her company Theranos' capabilities and defrauded people out of millions, which landed her in the clink. So, her staring at Fielder, talking about how she wouldn't deceive him? Yeah, it feels a little like you're looking at a female Hannibal Lecter with a more socially acceptable diet. The three-hour documentary got rave reviews in its surprise screening, but more importantly, it birthed a slew of memes. Well, I think I'll have to clear a couple of hours and check that puppy out when it comes out in October. And if you've never seen "Nathan For You," you probably have a friend who will talk your ear off about it. We've got a new burrito-eating queen, and her name is this lady I used to be a big Guinness Book of World Records guy when it was all about fat motorcycle twins and people clipping dozens of clothespins to their face, but it's gotten a little ridiculous. Most of the time it's just people doing things that no one ever really thought to do before, and are therefore records. Like, I could balance a few books on the end of a plunger and — voila! — record. So, it made me happy to see an old-school-style record courtesy of Great Britain's Leah Shutkever. That record? Housing a burrito faster than any human being ever has before... when being filmed on camera by the people from Guinness. Did anyone else just think of some David Attenborough-narrated nature documentary where a python swallows an antelope whole, or was that just me? What a display, and nice to see the British loosening up a little on the manners front. Tough to be on the forefront of competitive eating if you're more concerned with which fork goes where instead of cramming tortilla, rice, and beans into your food hole. SUBSCRIBE TO 'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW' ON YOUTUBE Congratulations, Leah. We can't wait to see what you gorge yourself on next. Fake dog's fake dog list divides the internet. In my humble opinion, one of the greatest bits of the last 35 years is Triumph the Insult Comic Dog. The brainchild of comedy great Robert Smigel, I can throw on a Triumph bit from "Late Night" that I've already seen dozens of times and laugh hysterically like it's brand new. It's genius. However, Triumph may have taken a wrong step, and it was all because of his tier list of TV and movie dogs. He's No. 1 — which I can live with — but after that, things get wild. That's a great list... for me and the rest of the internet to poop on! Wishbone on the same tier as Scrappy-Doo? One is a Jack Russell Terrier who exposed a generation to literary classics, while the other is Scooby's nephew that everyone hates. And Air Bud in the "Near Great" tier? Did I imagine this, or is he a multi-sport athlete who has bailed out multiple teams over the years? Those are my gripes; others had theirs. There are also a few omissions I think we need to include. First is Muttley of "Wacky Races" fame, who I think needs to go in the average tier. Not a bad sidekick for Dick Dastardly, but could've been near-great had he helped him pull off more evil schemes successfully. The other one is Tiger from "The Brady Bunch," who was an abject failure. Do you realize how bad you have to be to get written out of "The Brady Bunch" when they chose to write in Cousin Oliver? ... CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That's it for today's edition of Nightcaps! See you tomorrow!

articles.title: College Football All-Week 1 Team: Darian Mensah, Malachi Toney Show Out
articles.summary: From historic 7-TD passing performances to record-breaking receiving marks by an 18-year-old, check out the CFB Week 1 All-Star Team.
articles.body: Week 1 of the college football season is in the books, and what a week it was. From thrilling and controversial finishes to stunning upsets and incredible individual performances, the opening week delivered plenty of memorable moments. A pair of Miami superstars delivered record-breaking performances while Jayden Maiava and Jeremiah Smith put their names right into the Heisman conversation. With that, let's dive into the top offensive performances from Week 1 of the CFB season. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports. QB Darian Mensah In his first start with the Hurricanes, Darian Mensah balled out. He finished Friday night's win over Stanford with 401 passing yards and five touchdowns, becoming just the sixth quarterback since 2000 to complete at least 90% of his passes while throwing for 400-plus yards and five touchdowns in a game. After his dominant Week 1 performance, Mensah is now the favorite to win the Heisman Trophy at +600. No player's stock went up more than Mensah in Week 1. QB Mason Heintschel In Week 1 against Miami Ohio, Pittsburgh quarterback Mason Heintschel completed 31 of 41 passes for 453 yards and seven touchdowns. Yes, seven. Heintschel became just the 26th player in college football since 2000 to throw for at least 450 yards and seven touchdowns in a game, leading Pitt to a dominant 59-14 win and a dream start to the 2026 season. Heintschel introduced himself to the college football world on Saturday and immediately put his name on the map. QB Jayden Maiava In Week 1 against Fresno State, Jayden Maiava completed 23 of 25 passes for 349 yards and three touchdowns, leading USC to a dominant 39-0 win. His 92% completion rate was the highest in USC history in a game with at least 25 pass attempts and the second-highest overall with at least 20 attempts, trailing only Matt Barkley's 95% mark in 2012. Maiava's performance also tied for the 10th-highest completion percentage in an FBS game with at least 25 attempts and 300 passing yards since 2000. The Trojans' quarterback has put himself right into the Heisman race as his odds sit at +1750 to win the award. RB, Kamari Moulton Against Northern Illinois, Iowa running back Kamari Moulton rushed 11 times for 183 yards and two touchdowns, averaging a ridiculous 16.64 yards per carry. The senior set an Iowa single-game record for yards per carry with at least 10 attempts, shattering Fred Russell's previous mark of 12.14 in 2002. Moulton's 16.64 yards per carry also ranks fifth among Big Ten players since 2000 with at least 10 carries in a game. His 183 rushing yards are tied for the 10th-most by an FBS player on 11 or fewer carries since 2000. RB Jaylin Carter Jaylin Carter rushed 19 times for 183 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 9.63 yards per carry, while adding an 18-yard reception to finish with 201 total yards. Carter became just the fifth player in Tigers program history to rush for at least four touchdowns in a single game. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Carter has already racked up 280 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 34 carries, averaging an impressive 8.24 yards per carry. RB Nate Sheppard Against Tulane, Duke running back Nate Sheppard rushed 35 times for 227 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 6.49 yards per carry. His 227 rushing yards were the most by any FBS player in Week 1 of the 2026 season. After earning second-team All-ACC honors and rushing for more than 1,000 yards last season, Sheppard looks poised for another big year in the Blue Devils' backfield. WR Malachi Toney On Friday night, Malachi Toney hauled in 12 catches for 234 yards and three touchdowns against Stanford, setting Miami's single-game receiving yards record. The historic performance continued Toney's incredible start to his college career after he led the FBS with 109 receptions as a true freshman last season and set Miami's single-season receiving yards record with 1,211, surpassing Charleston Rambo's previous mark of 1,172 in 2021. Toney hit the Heisman pose three teams as his odds to win the award surged after Week 1 from +4000 to +1250. WR Deuce Alexander In Ole Miss' 41-38 win over No. 24 Louisville, senior wide receiver Deuce Alexander hauled in five catches for a career-high 159 yards and two touchdowns. Alexander caught two 62-yard touchdown passes in the third quarter, providing a major spark to the Ole Miss offense in the second half. His 31.8 yards per reception are tied for the third-highest single-game average in Ole Miss history among players with at least five catches. After his explosive Week 1 performance, Alexander looks poised for a massive season as Trinidad Chambliss' No. 1 target. WR Jeremiah Smith Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in Ohio State's dominant win over Ball State, with all of his production coming in the first half. His 151 receiving yards were the second-most he's recorded in a first half, trailing only the 161 he had against Oregon in the 2025 Rose Bowl. Smith now has 29 career receiving touchdowns, six more than any other college football player since 2024. He also recorded his 12th career 100-yard receiving game, passing Chris Olave for the second-most by an Ohio State player since 2000 and trailing only Marvin Harrison Jr. (15). Smith will have a real chance to break that mark in 2026 as he continues to show why he's the best receiver in the country. Smith currently has the third-best odds to win the Heisman at +1000.

articles.title: Aaron Judge Back In Yankees Lineup Following 99-Day Rib Injury Absence
articles.summary: Aaron Judge is returning to the New York Yankees after a 99-day absence caused by a broken rib, starting in right field and batting third against the Colorado Rockies.
articles.body: Aaron Judge returned to the New York Yankees after a 99-day absence caused by a broken rib, starting in right field and batting third Tuesday night against the Colorado Rockies. A three-time AL MVP, Judge had missed 84 games since his last appearance on May 31. The 34-year-old skipped a minor league injury rehabilitation assignment. Judge entered hitting .248 with 17 homers, 38 RBIs and a .907 OPS. He was initially injured attempting to avoid second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. during an unsuccessful try for a diving catch at Houston on April 26 and batted .263 with seven homers and 20 RBIs in 31 games before going on the injured list. He had just one homer in 18 games before the IL stint. New York was 36-23 after Judge last played on May 31 and went 45-39 in his absence. The Yankees hit .243 with 86 homers and a .770 OPS in 59 games through May 31 but .227 with 107 homers and a .681 OPS while Judge was sidelined. Their batting average during that stretch ranked 29th among the 30 major league teams, ahead of Seattle at .225. New York entered 81-62, four games behind of AL East-leading Tampa Bay and two games in front of Boston (80-65) for the top AL wild card. The Yankees hold a potential tiebreaker over the Red Sox after winning the season series. Judge hit a career-high .331 with 53 homers and 114 RBIs in 152 games last year, winning his third MVP and first batting title. He missed 10 games from July 26 to Aug. 4 with a flexor strain in his right elbow that he sustained on a throw to home plate July 22 in Toronto. He underwent a plasma-rich platelet injection and did not require offseason surgery. Judge skipped a rehab assignment in 2023 when he missed 42 games with a fractured right big toe after crashing into the right-field fence at Dodger Stadium. He hit .245 with 18 homers, 35 RBIs and a .965 OPS over 57 games after his return. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Hawkeye Marching Band Member Passes Away Following Heat Related Cardiac Arrest at Kinnick Stadium
articles.summary: Derek Phillips, a member of the Hawkeye Marching band has tragically passed away after suffering a heat related cardiac arrest during Iowa’s game against Nor...
articles.body:
Saturday's season opener between the Iowa Hawkeyes and Northern Illinois Huskies was an absolute scorcher. Temperatures were in the mid-90s throughout the day with a heat index over 100. Temps on the field at Kinnick Stadium, where heat radiates off the turf, were several degrees warmer.

Throughout the game, fans were encouraged to seek shade and stay hydrated. As halftime approached, we learned that due to the heat, there would be no halftime performance by the Hawkeye Marching Band or the dance team.

Today our staff, along with many of you, is incredibly saddened to learn the absence of the halftime show was not simply a precaution. Shortly before the end of the first half, a member of the Hawkeye Marching Band suffered cardiac arrest and was taken to the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics.

This morning his family reported making the difficult decision to remove life support after his brain was damaged from the incident.

His name was Derek Phillips. He was a student of the University of Iowa in his third year with the Hawkeye Marching Band. He played mellophone and was also a member of the prestigious and selective Colts Drum and Bugle Corps.

In a statement posted to social media his family expressed heartbreak while remembering fondly his love of music.

There are multiple staff members here at BHGP who are proud HMB alumni. The HMB is a special group with myriad traditions and inside jokes. It's a fraternity of sorts, a common thread that connects so many people from so many different eras. Derek was a part of that thread. He was a part of a cherished gameday tradition that brings joy and pageantry to gameday at Kinnick stadium.

We send our heartfelt condolences to all those who knew him.

articles.title: Cameron Heyward says this season or next will be his last
articles.summary: Steelers defensive lineman Cameron Heyward is 37 and entering his 16th season.
articles.body:
Steelers defensive lineman Cameron Heyward is 37 and entering his 16th season. He has shown no signs of a dropoff, playing all 17 games each of the past two seasons and earning first-team and second-team All-Pro honors respectively.

But Heyward knows the end his coming . . . and soon.

Heyward said on The Rich Eisen Show that either 2026 or 2027 will be his final season. His contract runs through 2027.

"I don't think it's it," Heyward said, via Aaron Becker of steelersnow.com. "You've got to see how the body feels. I've got 17 games, hopefully more , in me. We'll see how we do after this long playoff run we have. I don't like to jump the gun, but I will say, if this is not my last year, next year will definitely be my last year, because, I have to say, we're not signing anymore contracts after this."

The Steelers drafted the heir apparent in 2025, using a first-round pick on Derrick Harmon .

Heyward still totaled 78 tackles, 3.5 sacks, a forced fumble and six passes defensed. Harmon recorded three sacks, five quarterback hits, 27 tackles and a pass defensed in 12 games with eight starts.

articles.title: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing Dolphins' Week 1 game with Raiders Wire
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins will take on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1, so we took the time to speak with Raiders Wire's Levi Damien to get some inside info.
articles.body:
After a long offseason filled with many changes to the roster, coaching staff and front office, followed by an 0-3 preseason run, the Miami Dolphins are ready to begin their 2026 campaign.

Miami will play their first game of the season on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, as they'll take on the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. Last year, the Raiders finished with a 3-14 record, which was tied for the worst in the NFL, while the Dolphins finished 7-10.

As we look ahead to this matchup, we spoke to Raiders Wire lead writer Levi Damien to get some a better idea about who Miami will take on in Week 1.

Why do you think the Raiders ultimately chose to ride with Kirk Cousins in Week 1?

"First off, that was the plan from the start. Cousins was familiar with Klint Kubiak's scheme because he worked with him before in Minnesota . The team always hoped to not have to rush Fernando Mendoza into the lineup if he wasn't ready. Mendoza would have had to burst onto the scene in camp and preseason while Cousins struggled. Neither of those happened. Quite the contrary actually. Cousins looked great and Mendoza, while showing flashes, is not ready yet." -- LD

What is Klint Kubiak bringing to Las Vegas that's different than Pete Carroll?

"They are very different. Carroll is a defensive guy. He's also exuberant and constantly tried to have fun with his players and was 74 years old. Kubiak is an offensive guy, he's quiet and very business-like and 39 years old. Carroll's failings were probably more to do with the game passing him by. Kubiak's cutting edge, while also having the expertise of being a second generation football coach." -- LD

Who is an under-the-radar player that Dolphins fans should know about before this meeting?

"I'll go with DT Tonka Hemingway . He came on strong late last season as a rookie and the new coaching staff is really high on him. Throughout camp and preseason, he was the one interior defensive lineman who seemed to never be rotated out with the first team. Always on the field while they rotated the other position." -- LD

If you could add one former Los Angeles/Oakland/ Las Vegas Raiders player to this team to help them in this matchup, who would you choose?

"The Raiders are desperate for an X receiver. But since Randy Moss was a POS during his time in Oakland, let's flip to the other side of the ball and go with Charles Woodson . Preferably from his first stint when he was still playing cornerback." -- LD

Who do you think will win this game and why?

"I see the Dolphins starting a tank season. And since the Raiders had theirs already, they'll be happy to help Miami get things started off on the right foot. Raiders 20, Dolphins 13" -- LD

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Fever Teammates Rally Around Her After Spectacular FIBA World Cup Debut
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark is making her Fever teammates proud by repping the team on an international stage in the World Cup. Clark made a major splash in the tournament...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark is making her Fever teammates proud by repping the team on an international stage in the World Cup. Clark made a major splash in the tournament, with her debut game against Team China showing an absolute behemoth of a performance.

Clark and Team USA gave China a run for their money, with the Indy icon chalking up a sweet fourteen on the board, with eleven helpers. The game was clearly one for the debutantes, with Clark, Paige Bueckers and Rhyne Howard all etching an equal number of points on the board.

Soon after the win, Clark shared a few pictures from the game against China, which got the attention of her Indiana teammates back in the United States. Clark, of course, managed to sneak in a couple of pictures of her Nike shoe line, being the good ambassador she is.

"Grateful (red heart emoji) @usabasketball," Caitlin Clark wrote in her Instagram post. "Mamacita," Raven Johnson commented. "Global GOAT," Makayla Timpson added.

"Grateful (red heart emoji) @usabasketball," Caitlin Clark wrote in her Instagram post.

Raven Johnson's comment on Caitlin Clark 's post definitely got heads turning, especially for those who remember all the hue-and-cry by Fever fans when she signed with Indiana. Johnson openly called out Clark and her fans after an NCAA Final Four game, during which she was waved off.

The same fans did not like the Fever bringing Johnson into the fold, with many being worried about how the chemistry between Raven and Clark will turn out to be. However, looking at their interactions and also Johnson hyping Clark up for her Team USA performance, it looks like the two players are getting along just fine.

Caitlin Clark Stinks In Second Game Against Italy

Caitlin Clark thankfully got an easy team in China for her debut. Playing against a Li-Yueru-less China gave Team USA a super-easy win, with the matchup being incredibly beneficial for Clark and the other debutantes of the team. China had a big height advantage in Zhang Ziyu, something that the Americans lacked. Despite this, Clark and her teammate kicked off their World Cup journey with a splendid performance.

However, soon after the win against China, Team USA ran into trouble with Italy. The American ladies barely scraped a win against the Italians, with Clark's performance being among the worst. Clark etched up a measly 'one' on the board, something which has got a lot of criticism since the game. Hopefully, the Indy star will turn the narrative around as the team gets ready to take on the Czech Republic next up.

articles.title: Bengals’ Joe Burrow gets an MVP nod from fan-favorite personality
articles.summary: Some national chatter really likes Bengals QB Joe Burrow for MVP.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is one of the better MVP projections going into the regular season.

Not hard to see why. He's healthy and surrounded not just by Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, but bonuses like the same starting five offensive linemen for the first time in his career. Also, for the first time in his career, his front office is all-in through modern means.

Hence, someone like Kay Adams predicting Burrow will take home the award.

"I think Joe Burrow wins MVP. He knows it's go-time," Adams said. "He's measured that way. He's dialed in. Sort of on another level. He always is, but there's more balance to it. He talked to me about mind, body, and soul. He's never talked like that to me before."

Adams, a fan favorite to the point of being "Ruler of the Jungle" at Paycor Stadium years ago, will find plenty of fans happy about this one.

And as always, Bengals fans know the drill: If Burrow is healthy, which is always the big question, the Bengals are probably contending in a big way if he's in the MVP race.

articles.title: Tim Couch, Craig Yeast are honorary captains for Kentucky vs. Alabama
articles.summary: Kentucky football legends Tim Couch and Craig Yeast will be honorary captains vs. Alabama on Saturday, Sept. 12. They teamed up to beat Bama in 1997.
articles.body:
LEXINGTON — The honorary captains for Kentucky football on Saturday, Sept. 12, are familiar faces to the fanbase.

Quarterback Tim Couch and wide receiver Craig Yeast connected on a 26-yard touchdown in overtime to knock off Alabama 40-34 at then- Commonwealth Stadium in 1997. Now, nearly 30 years later, Couch and Yeast will be together again as honorary captains as the Wildcats prepare to host the Crimson Tide at Kroger Field .

The 1997 victory marked UK's last win in the series ; its only other triumph over UA was in 1922.

Arguably the best signal caller in program history , Couch still holds numerous single-game, single-season and career records at Kentucky . Yeast is at the top of the school's list in numerous career categories, including receptions (208), receiving yards (2,899) and receiving touchdowns (28).

Saturday's game will kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET and air nationally on ABC.

SEC Nation will conduct its pregame show from 9 a.m. to noon, live from campus.

articles.title: ‘Anything But Mid’ Podcast: Big Sky, Big South and Big West Men’s Basketball Preview
articles.summary: Montana State, High Point and UC San Diego appear to be early favorites
articles.body:
This week on our podcast, "Anything But Mid," we spoke about the Big Sky, Big South and Big West for men's basketball.

The Big Sky is welcoming Southern Utah and Utah Tech for the upcoming 2026-2027 season. This is an action-packed, tightly competitive conference, so having two new teams can shake things up this season. Portland State comes in as the defending champs, but losing players like Terri Miller Jr. and Tre-Vaughn Minott will hurt the program. Similarly, defending tournament champion Idaho lost important pieces during the offseason. Montana State seems to be an early favorite. After going 12-6 in conference, the Bobcats retain pretty much their entire core and all 10 scholarship players. Cavin Holden will be fully healthy after a season-ending injury while Jed Miller looks to have another breakout year with Montana State.

This seems to be High Point's conference to lose. The Panthers have won the conference tournament two years in a row and are in a prime position to three-peat. Flynn Clayman is one of the top coaches in the country. Key returners in Cam'Ron Fletcher and Conrad Martinez combined with transfers Jason Rivera Torres, Isaac Garrett and CJ Brown makes High Point just as scary as last year. Winthrop will still continue to compete after going 13-3 in conference last season, but High Point is the odds on favorite as of today.

Talk about a realignment. The conference lost UC Davis and reigning champion Hawaii to the Mountain West while adding California Baptist, Sacramento State and Utah Valley. These moves shape up to affect the top of the conference as Hawaii won the title and Cal Baptist and Utah Valley met in the WAC championship last season. UC Irvine lost to Hawaii in the Big West Championship last season but lost some key pieces Jurian Dixon, Derin Saran and Kyle Evans in the offseason. UC San Diego, who's leaving for the WCC next season, looks to be an early favorite. The Tritons added transfers Treysen Eaglestaff from West Virginia and Camp Wagner from Indiana State along with key returners Leo Beath and Alex Chaikin.

Make sure to tune into the "Anything But Mid" Podcast on Apple Podcasts and Spotify and stay tuned for our women's basketball preview for these conferences!

articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers could have another weapon ready to emerge from their backfield in 2026, and rookie Kaelon Black may be the player who gives fans a re...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers could have another weapon ready to emerge from their backfield in 2026, and rookie Kaelon Black may be the player who gives fans a reason to believe the running game can become even deeper. A bold projection for the first-year running back calls for a workload that would signal a meaningful shift in how San Francisco manages its offense.

The prediction has Black recording at least 650 rushing yards during his rookie season, a total that would represent a substantial contribution behind Christian McCaffrey . Such production would require the 49ers to rely less heavily on McCaffrey while giving their young runner regular opportunities to establish himself within Kyle Shanahan's offense.

Black arrived in San Francisco as the 90th overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft after helping Indiana complete a national championship season. He finished his final college campaign with 1,039 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, bringing a physical running style and the versatility needed to fit into an offense that has consistently demanded multiple skills from its backs.

The rookie has already shown flashes of the traits that made him an appealing selection. His ability to run through contact, find extra yardage and attack openings with urgency could make him a useful complement to McCaffrey, particularly in situations where the 49ers want to preserve their star's workload over a long season.

San Francisco 49ers Rookie Kaelon Black Receives Bold Prediction Ahead of 2026 NFL Season

Black received a major prediction for the upcoming NFL season. This is detailed more in an analysis by Seth Walder for ESPN.

Bold prediction for 2026: Rookie running back Kaelon Black will record at least 650 rushing yards as the 49ers — for real this time — take it easy on Christian McCaffrey's workload. That would be 250 more rushing yards than last year's backup running back, Brian Robinson Jr.

A lighter workload for McCaffrey could ultimately benefit both players and the offense as a whole. San Francisco has experienced the consequences of injuries and attrition in recent seasons, and developing a dependable secondary option would give Shanahan greater flexibility while keeping one of the league's most important offensive players fresher for the games that matter most.

Black still faces the challenge of earning consistent touches in a crowded backfield, but the opportunity is clearly there for a rookie capable of making the most of limited chances. If the bold prediction becomes reality, the 49ers will have found more than a promising young backup, as Black could become an important part of an offense built to keep San Francisco among the NFC's most dangerous teams.
